title: Travel and subsistence approval
statement: Travel or subsistence spend above £500 requires written approval from the relevant budget owner before booking. An item must not be split into smaller transactions to avoid the threshold. The claimant must submit an itemised receipt and business purpose within ten calendar days after the trip.
summary: Travel spend above £500 needs advance budget-owner approval, and claims need receipts within ten days.

questions.question: Who must approve travel costing more than £500?
questions.answer: The relevant budget owner must give written approval before the booking.

questions.question: Can an employee split a £700 booking into two claims?
questions.answer: No. A transaction must not be split to avoid the £500 approval threshold.

questions.question: When must a travel receipt be submitted?
questions.answer: An itemised receipt and business purpose must be submitted within ten calendar days after the trip.

questions.question: Does a £450 hotel booking need the special threshold approval?
questions.answer: The special written pre-approval rule applies only when travel or subsistence spend is above £500, although normal booking controls still apply.

title: Supplier invoice payment clock
statement: A valid supplier invoice is payable thirty calendar days after Finance receives it. The invoice must quote an approved purchase order unless Procurement has recorded an exception. When an invoice is formally disputed, the payment clock pauses until the supplier supplies the missing or corrected information.
summary: Valid supplier invoices are due in thirty days, require a purchase order, and pause while formally disputed.

questions.question: What is the normal supplier invoice payment term?
questions.answer: A valid supplier invoice is payable thirty calendar days after Finance receives it.

questions.question: Must a supplier invoice include a purchase order?
questions.answer: Yes, it must quote an approved purchase order unless Procurement has recorded an exception.

questions.question: What happens to the payment clock during an invoice dispute?
questions.answer: The payment clock pauses until the supplier provides the missing or corrected information.

questions.question: Does the thirty-day clock start when the supplier sends the invoice?
questions.answer: It starts when Finance receives a valid invoice, not merely when the supplier sends it.

title: Annual leave and carry-over
statement: A full-time employee receives twenty-five days of annual leave in addition to public holidays. Leave requires manager approval before commitments are made. Up to five unused days may be carried into the next leave year and must be used by 31 March unless HR approves an exceptional extension.
summary: Employees receive twenty-five leave days, need manager approval, and may carry five days until 31 March.

questions.question: How many annual leave days does a full-time employee receive?
questions.answer: A full-time employee receives twenty-five annual leave days in addition to public holidays.

questions.question: Can leave be booked before manager approval?
questions.answer: No. Manager approval is required before commitments are made.

questions.question: How many leave days can be carried over?
questions.answer: Up to five unused days may be carried into the next leave year.

questions.question: By when must carried leave normally be used?
questions.answer: It must normally be used by 31 March unless HR approves an exceptional extension.

title: Hybrid working baseline
statement: Eligible employees may work remotely for up to three days in a normal working week when team coverage is maintained. They must be reachable during the core collaboration period from 10:00 to 15:00 UK time. Confidential information may be handled remotely only on a company-managed device through the approved secure connection.
summary: Eligible staff may work remotely three days, keep core hours, and use managed secure devices for confidential data.

questions.question: How many remote-working days are normally allowed?
questions.answer: Eligible employees may work remotely for up to three days in a normal working week when team coverage is maintained.

questions.question: What are the core collaboration hours?
questions.answer: Employees must be reachable from 10:00 to 15:00 UK time.

questions.question: Can confidential information be handled on a personal laptop at home?
questions.answer: No. Confidential information may be handled remotely only on a company-managed device through the approved secure connection.

questions.question: Is remote work allowed when team coverage would be lost?
questions.answer: No. The three-day baseline applies only when team coverage is maintained.

title: Production release gate
statement: A production release requires passing automated tests, a completed security scan, a named release owner, and a documented rollback plan. A change classified as high risk additionally requires approval from two people who did not author the change. Evidence for every gate must be linked in the release record before deployment begins.
summary: Production releases need test, security, ownership and rollback evidence; high-risk changes need two independent approvals.

questions.question: What evidence is required for every production release?
questions.answer: It needs passing automated tests, a completed security scan, a named release owner, a documented rollback plan, and links to the evidence in the release record.

questions.question: How is a high-risk release approved?
questions.answer: It requires approval from two people who did not author the change, in addition to the normal release gates.

questions.question: Can deployment start before evidence links are added?
questions.answer: No. Evidence for every gate must be linked in the release record before deployment begins.

questions.question: Is a rollback plan optional for a low-risk production release?
questions.answer: No. A documented rollback plan is required for every production release.

title: Severity-one incident response
statement: An incident is severity one when it creates a credible safety risk, confirmed material data loss, or a complete customer-facing service outage. The on-call lead must appoint an incident commander within fifteen minutes of confirmation. A written post-incident review is due within five working days and must identify owners for corrective actions.
summary: Safety risk, material data loss or full outage is severity one; appoint a commander in fifteen minutes and review in five days.

questions.question: What conditions make an incident severity one?
questions.answer: A credible safety risk, confirmed material data loss, or a complete customer-facing service outage makes an incident severity one.

questions.question: How quickly must an incident commander be appointed?
questions.answer: The on-call lead must appoint an incident commander within fifteen minutes of confirmation.

questions.question: When is the post-incident review due?
questions.answer: A written post-incident review is due within five working days.

questions.question: What must the post-incident review include?
questions.answer: It must identify owners for corrective actions.

title: Customer support first-response targets
statement: Priority-one customer cases require a human first response within fifteen minutes and continuous ownership until stabilisation. Priority-two cases require a first response within two business hours. Priority-three cases require a first response by the end of the next business day. Automated acknowledgements do not count as a human first response.
summary: Support targets are fifteen minutes for P1, two business hours for P2, and next business day for P3.

questions.question: What is the P1 first-response target?
questions.answer: A priority-one customer case requires a human first response within fifteen minutes and continuous ownership until stabilisation.

questions.question: What is the P2 first-response target?
questions.answer: A priority-two case requires a first response within two business hours.

questions.question: What is the P3 first-response target?
questions.answer: A priority-three case requires a first response by the end of the next business day.

questions.question: Does an automated acknowledgement satisfy the response target?
questions.answer: No. Automated acknowledgements do not count as a human first response.

title: New supplier onboarding
statement: A new supplier must complete identity, bank-account, sanctions, and conflict-of-interest checks before a purchase order is issued. A supplier handling company or customer data must also complete the security questionnaire and sign the approved data-processing terms. The requester may not approve the supplier's own bank details.
summary: New suppliers need identity, bank, sanctions and conflict checks; data suppliers also need security and processing terms.

questions.question: Which checks are required before issuing a purchase order to a new supplier?
questions.answer: Identity, bank-account, sanctions, and conflict-of-interest checks must be completed first.

questions.question: What extra controls apply when a supplier handles data?
questions.answer: The supplier must complete the security questionnaire and sign the approved data-processing terms.

questions.question: Can the requester approve the supplier's bank details?
questions.answer: No. The requester may not approve the supplier's own bank details.

questions.question: May a purchase order be issued before the sanctions check?
questions.answer: No. All required onboarding checks, including sanctions, must be complete before a purchase order is issued.

title: Restricted cryptographic recovery procedure
statement: This synthetic record represents security material that must remain outside broadly accessible model weights and is intentionally excluded from compilation unless an explicit governance override is supplied.
summary: Restricted security knowledge excluded from model-weight training.
